newsitem.title: USA: Israel's Mordechai urges Arafat-Netanyahu meeting.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Mordechai urges Arafat-Netanyahu meeting.

text.p: Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai on Wednesday accused the Palestinian Authority of failing to honour the Hebron agreement and urged a meeting soon between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to end the latest round of violence.

Mordechai, starting a visit to the United States that will include talks in Washington with senior Clinton administration officials, said the violence of the last two weeks had to end before the peace process could move forward.
"What we need is all the clever men, all the leaders (to) make a decision, a basic decision to fight against terrorism," Mordechai said after briefing a U.S. Jewish group in New York.

"At the same time Chairman Arafat will have (to make) his best effort to fight against the violence in the area and have a meeting with Prime Minister Benjamnin Netanyahu to find a formula on how to continue with the peace process, to create a different atmosphere in the area."

Mordechai told the Conference of Presidents of Major American Jewish Organisations that Israel had followed "100 percent" January's accord that started Palestinian self-rule and Israeli withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron.
He accused the Palestinian Authority, created under the 1993 Israel-PLO peace agreements, of failing to keep its end of the bargain.

"Almost every day, every week, I make sure that our military forces respect the agreement but unfortunately the Palestinians don't have all the respect, everything that is necessary to follow that has been signed with us," said Mordechai, without being specific.

Violence has flared for two weeks in the West Bank since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu broke ground on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem. The violence has worsened even as President Bill Clinton has held talks with the leaders of Israeli, Egypt, the Palestinians and Jordan.

Mordechai had meetings scheduled in Washington on Thursday and Friday with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen and U.S. National Security Advisor Sandy Berger, the Israeli Embassy in Washington said. Clinton will meet Netanyahu in Washington on Monday for talks on saving Israeli-Palestinian peace negotiations.
